description: Massive, awe-inspiring ruins of an 8th-century Hindu temple dedicated to Surya.
history: Built by King Lalitaditya Muktapida of the Karkota dynasty, it stands as a testament to the architectural brilliance of ancient Kashmir before its eventual destruction.

description: The remains of two 9th-century Hindu temples featuring intricate stone carvings.
history: Situated on the banks of the Jhelum River, these temples were built by King Awantivarman, dedicated to Lord Vishnu and Lord Shiva.

description: A seven-terraced Mughal garden and historical monument overlooking Dal Lake.
history: Built in the mid-1600s by Mughal Prince Dara Shikoh, it originally served as a library, an observatory, and a spiritual retreat.

description: An imposing fortification sitting on a hill above Srinagar.
history: While the site's fortification dates back to the Mughal era under Akbar, the current structure was heavily built upon by the Durrani Empire in the 18th century.

description: A highly restricted but accessible valley famous for its pyramid-shaped Habba Khatoon peak.
history: Located close to the Line of Control, it preserves the unique, ancient Dard-Shina indigenous culture and was historically part of the ancient Silk Route.

description: A massive, untouched biosphere and alpine meadow in the Kupwara district.
history: Surrounded by the Shamsabari and Leepa mountain ranges, it remains one of the most pristine and unexplored ecological zones in Kashmir.

description: A quiet, completely off-grid destination in South Kashmir with pine forests and streams.
history: Often referred to as a 'mini Pahalgam' without the commercialization, offering raw natural beauty.

description: An oval-shaped valley known for its vast fruit orchards and natural springs.
history: Besides its natural beauty, the valley is home to the mysterious ancient Kalaroos caves, which local legends suggest connect all the way to Russia.

description: The summer capital of Jammu and Kashmir, famous for Dal Lake and houseboats.
history: Founded by King Pravarasena II over 2,000 years ago, it became a major hub under the Mughal Empire, resulting in the creation of the famous UNESCO-listed terraced gardens.

description: The premier ski resort destination in India known as the 'Meadow of Flowers'.
history: Originally named Gaurimarg by shepherds, it was renamed by the 16th-century Sultan Yusuf Shah. It now hosts one of the highest cable cars in the world.

description: The Valley of Shepherds, famous for its lush landscapes in Betaab and Aru Valley.
history: Historically a humble shepherd village, it has grown into a major tourism hub and serves as the traditional base camp for the ancient Amarnath Yatra pilgrimage.

description: A stunning trek to two massive, twin alpine lakes separated by a mountain.
history: A pristine natural route through the Aru Valley that has long been used by local Gujjar shepherds before becoming a popular modern trekking trail.

description: A challenging route tracing up the Lidder River to the highest glacier in Kashmir.
history: The Kolahoi Glacier is the main source of the Jhelum River system, making it historically and ecologically vital to the entire Kashmir valley.
